hero.headline: NO FAIRY-TALE ENDING
hero.standfirst: A 91st-minute goal by substitute Mikel Merino sent Spain through and ended Cristiano Ronaldo's last World Cup — and before the night was over, Belgium had routed the host nation 4–1 in Seattle. The bracket has lost its biggest name and its loudest crowd in one evening.
hero.photoCaption: Cristiano Ronaldo — 19 touches in his final World Cup match, by his own word his last

briefing.text: Crystal Ball, day one: the Spain call landed, the USA call didn't — the live market's 34% warning on Belgium aged very well.
USA, Mexico and Canada are all out — this World Cup will be lifted by a visiting nation.
Rest day tomorrow, then the quarter-finals begin Thursday in Boston with France–Morocco.

insideToday.text: Portugal 0–1 Spain — Merino's late dagger and Ronaldo's quiet goodbye
USA 1–4 Belgium — the hosts' dream dies loudly in Seattle
Tonight: Messi's champions meet Egypt, then Switzerland–Colombia closes the round
The Crystal Ball: tonight's calls, with live market prices — day one went 1 for 2
Golden Boot: three still tied on 7, and one of them plays tonight
The bracket: Spain–Belgium joins the quarter-final card

facts.text: Both goal-makers came off the bench: Ferran Torres slipped the pass, Merino finished at the near post
Ronaldo touched the ball just 19 times — his second-fewest in a World Cup match he started
Spain are still yet to concede a single goal at this World Cup

yesterday.report: For 90 minutes the Iberian derby was a chess game Portugal refused to lose — and then Luis de la Fuente's bench decided it. Ferran Torres, on in the second half, slipped a quick ball into the box in the 91st minute and Mikel Merino, the other substitute, buried it at the near post. Portugal never mustered a shot on target after the break.
yesterday.report2: It ends the international road of Cristiano Ronaldo, who had confirmed this would be his final tournament. Just 19 touches, the second-fewest of his World Cup career as a starter, while Rodri quietly ran the evening: 106 touches and 87 completed passes. Spain march into a Friday quarter-final against Belgium having still not conceded a goal.

star.name: Mikel Merino
star.line: On the pitch for the finish that settled a derby of fine margins — a near-post strike in the 91st minute, seconds after his fellow substitute created it.

aside.name: Ronaldo, 41
aside.line: Five World Cups, and a last one that ended with a whimper rather than a roar. He leaves the stage with the tournament still missing from his shelf.

yesterday.whatItMeans: Spain meet Belgium in Friday's Los Angeles quarter-final (18:00). Portugal's golden generation era closes without the one trophy it wanted most.

facts.text: De Ketelaere's second came barely a minute after Tillman's free kick had levelled the mood
Goalkeeper Matt Freese's mistake gifted Belgium their third early in the second half
The 'flat and leggy' Belgium of the group stage produced their sharpest 90 minutes of the tournament

yesterday.report: The night Seattle had waited a generation for lasted nine minutes. Charles De Ketelaere finished a flowing move to silence 66,925, and though Malik Tillman's 31st-minute free kick briefly lit the stadium back up, De Ketelaere struck again 90 seconds later. The reinstated Folarin Balogun and the home attack managed just two shots on target all night.
yesterday.report2: Matt Freese's error handed Hans Vanaken the third just before the hour, and substitute Romelu Lukaku added a fourth in stoppage time. Belgium out-attempted the hosts 15–7 and looked, for the first time this tournament, like the team their squad list promises. The USMNT's home World Cup ends in the round of 16 — and with it, the last host standing is gone.

star.name: Charles De Ketelaere
star.line: Two goals in the opening 33 minutes, the second a dagger thrown 90 seconds after the hosts had found hope. The quiet man of Belgium's new generation owned the loudest room in the tournament.

aside.name: Malik Tillman
aside.line: His curled free kick was the USMNT's one moment of joy — and at 24, part of the core that will carry the lessons of this night to 2030.

yesterday.whatItMeans: Belgium meet unbeaten Spain in Friday's Los Angeles quarter-final. All three host nations are out before the last eight.

today.preview: The defending champions have won all four games, but the last one took 120 minutes against Cape Verde — and Egypt arrive from a penalty-shootout epic of their own against Australia, deep in the best World Cup in their history. Messi, 39, has scored seven of Argentina's eleven goals; Mohamed Salah carries just as much of Egypt's hopes.
watch: Messi can take the Golden Boot lead outright with his eighth
Two tired teams: both needed 120 minutes to survive the last 32

keyMan.name: Mohamed Salah
keyMan.line: Egypt's captain and talisman, leading his country through its best-ever World Cup — and the one player Argentina will genuinely fear.

factors.label: FORM
factors.text: Argentina have won all four games, but needed 120 minutes to shake off Cape Verde; Egypt survived Australia only on penalties after their own 120.

factors.label: HEAD-TO-HEAD
factors.text: Messi and Salah have never faced each other at a World Cup — Egypt missed 2022, and the 2018 draw kept them apart. A first, and possibly a last.

factors.label: FITNESS & FATIGUE
factors.text: Both sides went the full 120 in the last 32 on the same day, so the rest ledger is even — but Egypt also carried the emotional load of a shootout.

factors.label: WHERE THE MONEY IS
factors.text: Kalshi's live market ($1.5m traded) is emphatic: Argentina 72%, the draw 20%, Egypt just 9% in regulation. Nobody is betting on the fairy tale.

prediction.verdict: The champions have looked mortal for 120 minutes at a time, but never beatable. Egypt's block will hold for a while; Messi tends to decide what happens after that. Argentina, comfortably enough — and perhaps the outright Golden Boot lead with it.

today.preview: The round closes with a genuine clash of styles: Switzerland's disciplined, tactically rigid block against a Colombia side that wants the ball and attacks in waves of technique. Colombia edged Ghana to get here but sweat on striker Jhon Córdoba, who lasted only eight minutes of that game.
watch: Colombia's flair against a organised Swiss block — patience will be everything
The winner gets Argentina or Egypt in Sunday's Kansas City quarter-final

keyMan.name: Luis Díaz
keyMan.line: Colombia's most dangerous attacker — direct, relentless, and exactly the type to unpick a deep Swiss defence one duel at a time.

factors.label: FORM
factors.text: Colombia edged past Ghana in the last 32 and have grown into the tournament; Switzerland have ground their way here on structure and set pieces.

factors.label: THE MATCH-UP
factors.text: A pure clash of styles: Switzerland's disciplined, deep block against Colombia's aggressive, technical possession game. Patience against pressure.

factors.label: FITNESS & FATIGUE
factors.text: Colombia sweat on striker Jhon Córdoba, who lasted just eight minutes against Ghana before going off injured.

factors.label: WHERE THE MONEY IS
factors.text: The quietest market of the round (Kalshi, $378k): Colombia 43%, Switzerland 27% — and a round-high 32% on the draw. The money smells extra time.

prediction.verdict: The draw price is the story: a third of the market expects this level after 90 minutes. We take Colombia's extra quality to tell eventually — but if Córdoba is out and the Swiss block settles in, nobody should be surprised by penalties in Vancouver.
